title: The Cold War
description: The rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union, from 1947 to 1991

questions.question: Which two superpowers were the main rivals of the Cold War?
choices: The US and the Soviet Union
questions.explanation: The Cold War was a geopolitical rivalry between the United States and its allies and the Soviet Union and its allies.

questions.question: Who popularized the phrase 'Iron Curtain' in a 1946 speech?
questions.explanation: Winston Churchill made the phrase famous when he described an 'iron curtain' descending across Europe in his speech at Fulton, Missouri, in March 1946. He did not coin it: the image had been used earlier, including by Churchill himself in 1945.

questions.question: Which US program provided economic aid to rebuild Western Europe after WWII?
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan (1948) sent over $13 billion to help Western European economies recover. The Truman Doctrine was a policy of containing communism.

questions.question: In what year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explanation: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall in August 1961 to stop people escaping to West Berlin. It fell in November 1989.

questions.question: What 1962 crisis brought the US and USSR closest to nuclear war?
questions.explanation: In October 1962 the US discovered Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba. A 13-day standoff ended when the Soviets agreed to remove them.

questions.question: What was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957?
questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 launched on 4 October 1957, starting the Space Race. Explorer 1 was the first US satellite, launched in 1958.

questions.question: Which military alliance did the Soviet Union and its Eastern European allies form in 1955?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Pact was the Soviet bloc's answer to NATO. Comecon was an economic organization, not a military alliance.

questions.question: Which Soviet leader introduced the policies of glasnost and perestroika?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev introduced glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) in the mid-1980s.

questions.question: What did the term 'MAD' stand for in Cold War nuclear strategy?
questions.explanation: Mutually Assured Destruction held that a full nuclear attack by either side would lead to the destruction of both, so neither would start one.

questions.question: In what year was the Soviet Union dissolved, ending the Cold War?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union formally dissolved in December 1991, breaking into 15 independent states.
